notable_features.text: Modern Greek has a long continuous history, with its modern form emerging gradually from the fourth century AD onward rather than at a single sharp break, even though the fall of the Byzantine Empire in 1453 is often used as a symbolic dividing line. It has a relatively rich phoneme inventory of 41 sounds and marks an unusually high number of tense/aspect distinctions (7 WALS categories). Unlike many languages, it has no single dominant word order, allowing flexible arrangement of sentence elements.
